Tome six follows the same plan, printed at Paris by Lahure under Regnier's series. The edition promises review from the oldest printings and the author's copies. Notes, notices, and a glossary of striking words support the text throughout.

With the plays complete, Corneille the thinker steps forward in this volume, by the v1 account. His examinations of his own plays judge his craft with candor. His discourses treat tragedy, comedy, and the unities of time, place, and action. Practical and sharp, he explains choices that puzzled his critics. Playwrights and scholars still mine these pages for a master's view of how drama works.
